newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-A$ rise helps inflation, pressure exports - RBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-A$ rise helps inflation, pressure exports - RBA.

text.p: The rise in the Australian dollar had helped contain inflation but was pressuring domestic exporters and those competing with imports, Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Ian Macfarlane said on Thursday.

"While the higher currency has been helpful from an inflation perspective, it has put pressure on our export industries and those competing with imports," Macfarlane told a business dinner in Melbourne.
"The pressure will be particularly felt in those industries which have let their domestic cost structure move up too fast," he said.
"The popularity of Australian dollar investments ... has lifted our exchange rate appreciably at a time of subdued commodity prices," Macfarlane said.
The principal source of this inflow of funds had been the Japanese household investor who had sought alternatives to the near-zero returns on offer in Japan, he said.

The Australian dollar has risen almost 10 percent against the U.S. dollar this year to hit a six-year high in recent days and has jumped 19 percent on the Japanese yen to a four-year peak earlier on Thursday.
